correctness.rationale: For fixed real 0<tau<1, p sufficiently large, projective reduction plus anticommutation with quarter-turn and power-sum majorization reduce the global operator norm to a nonnegative slope s in [0,1]. On [tau,1] the derivative sign is governed by H_p(s)=s^(p-1)-tau-(1+tau s^(p-1))*((s-tau)/(1+tau s))^(p-1). The three stated eventual inequalities give H_p monotonicity, one zero s_p>s0=tau^(1/(p-1)), and exactly two maximizing real projective lines. Mean-value expansion yields displacement s_p-s0~s0(1+tau^2)*rho_p^(p-1)/(tau*(p-1)); since the single-row quotient U_p has a stationary maximum at s0, its logarithmic loss is lower order than rho_p^p/p. Thus nu_p/R_p-1~rho_p^p/p and lim p*(nu_p-R_p)/rho^p=(1+tau)*tau^((1+tau^2)/(1-tau^2)). The Xu–Liu Lp conclusion is conditional on their published exact identity. Independent numerical optimizer checks for several tau and finite p corroborate the root and strict lower-bound gap; double precision ceases to resolve exponentially tiny gaps, and is not relied on for the limit.
residual_risks: Real scalars, real p sufficiently large and tau fixed in (0,1), not uniform in tau.
